Intro: I watched the old royalty glut themselves, salivating over the untrimmed fat, rolling oil glistening down their chins.
But just beyond the doors of their gilded palaces, I watched street children grow into their skin with no muscles; just tendon, sinew, and bone.
The wealth within their walls could've pulled every single one of those children out of poverty, fed every hungry mouth.
But as small, emaciated bodies outside crawled into each other's arms for heat, the nauseating sound of chewing and slurping persisted.
How could they still want? After they ate their fill, they hoarded the leftovers and forced themselves to swallow just so someone else could not eat.
This city was too weak-willed to free itself. Someone had to step in and save them.
And now you stand in my way again, fraternizing with rebels who don't know what it means to be free.
It was a good attempt. I admire your blind faith in foolish resolve.
This is the end of the line for you.
